solution:
The correct answer is __**2) i - b, ii - c, iii - a, iv - d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ketone** uses the suffix **-one** indicating the presence of a carbonyl group (C=O).
 
• **Alkene** uses the suffix **-ene** indicating the presence of a carbon-carbon double bond (-C=C-).
 
• **Aldehyde** uses the suffix **-al** indicating the presence of a formyl group (-CHO).
 
• **Carboxylic acid** uses the suffix **-oic acid** indicating the presence of a carboxyl group (-COOH).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keto Group (C=O)**:

 
 
• Found in ketones, characterized by the carbonyl group bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• Example: Propanone (acetone), the simplest ketone.
 
 
 
• **Alkene Group (-C=C-)**:
 
 
• Alkenes are hydrocarbons with at least one carbon-carbon double bond.
 
• Example: Ethene (ethylene), used in the production of polyethylene.
 
 
 
• **Formyl Group (-CHO)**:
 
 
• Found in aldehydes, characterized by a carbonyl group bonded to at least one hydrogen atom.
 
• Example: Methanal (formaldehyde), used in the production of resins.
 
 
 
• **Carboxyl Group (-COOH)**:
 
 
• Found in carboxylic acids, characterized by a carbonyl and hydroxyl group attached to the same carbon.
 
• Example: Ethanoic acid (acetic acid), a key component of vinegar.
